Emma (perf): Heads-up — planning a multi-region load + failover run next Wed to validate recent kernel selection and batching changes. Goal: apples-to-apples latency/throughput and exercise KV cache warm/cold paths.
Noah (sre): SGTM. Which regions and traffic model?
Emma (perf): us-west1 / us-east4 / eu-west1. Two phases: 1) synthetic steady-state (synthetic traffic) 2) replay harness using 24h production trace (replay).
Kevin (ml): For apples-to-apples we need same model checkpoint & quant config across regions. Using model v2.3.1 (int8 quant profile A). No dynamic kernel toggles during a run.
Sophia (runtime): Confirmed — runtime will pin kernel selection per instance via KERNEL_PROFILE=stable. We'll record which kernel was chosen in profiler output.
Maria (qa): For KV cache behavior I recommend 3 cache states: cold (empty), warm (single user warm), and hot (100% cache hits). We'll run each for 10m and collect p50/p95/p99 + tail traces.
Emma (perf): Exactly. Metrics to capture: request latency histogram, tokens/sec, batch size distribution, KV hit rate, kernel name, cpu/gpu util, and heap/allocs. Also collect per-token timing from runtime profiler.
perf-bot: New profile created: gs://redwood-perf/multi-region/1711234567/run-meta.json : uploaded
Noah (sre): Load driver plan: k6 for synthetic; replayer v0.9 for trace replay. Example k6 job:
```
// loadtest.js
export default function() {
  http.post(URL, JSON.stringify({prompt: '...'}), {headers: {"Authorization": TOKEN}})
}
```
Run: k6 run --vus 300 --duration 15m --out influxdb=http://metrics:8086

Sophia (runtime): Important: disable autoscaling during run to keep instance kernel mapping stable. I'll set min=max for dedicated pools.
Kevin (ml): Note on batching heuristics — we should force continuous batching on for phase 1, and a 'per-request' mode for a controlled comparison. That way we can isolate batching gains.
Emma (perf): Good call. We'll have four combos per region: batching on/off × cache cold/hot. That yields neat apples-to-apples tables.
Maria (qa): For replay harness, I'll sanitize trace to remove personal data and normalize sequence length distribution (sampled) so each region gets same seq profile.
Noah (sre): Also doing a region-drain failover test: gradually drain us-west1 and route to us-east4. Measure added e2e latency and model fallback behavior if capacity constrained.
Sophia (runtime): Fallback rules: if model capacity < 20% of incoming, route to smaller model variant (v2.3.1-small). We'll measure quality delta separately.
Emma (perf): Quick profiling note: last week's kernel update (matmul_v4) caused a 12–18% p95 regression at seq>1024 in our internal smoke tests. We need to confirm if that's kernel selection or batching interaction.
Kevin (ml): I'll run a targeted microbenchmark: run identical workload with kernel pinned to matmul_v3 vs matmul_v4 and capture per-op timings + nvprof summaries.
perf-bot: microbench results uploaded: gs://redwood-perf/multi-region/1711234567/microbench-matmul_v3_v4.tar.gz
Noah (sre): If matmul_v4 is the culprit, for the run we should pin stable to v3 and annotate results. We can iterate later with kernel patch.
Emma (perf): Action items:
- Sophia: set instance kernel pinning + disable autoscale (due Tue EOD)
- Maria: prepare sanitized trace + cache-state harness (due Tue EOD)
- Kevin: microbench matmul_v3 vs v4 and upload artifacts (due Tue EOD)
- Noah: prepare k6 and replayer runners and influx buckets (due Tue EOD)
- I'll create the result dashboard template and SLO checks.
Sophia (runtime): I'll also enable verbose per-request profiler sampling (1%) to capture tail cause stacks without high overhead.
Kevin (ml): If we see consistent regression, propose regression label in commit history and revert path ready in case we need quick rollback.
Maria (qa): One more: include client-side RTT baseline from each region to our API frontends so we can separate network vs runtime.
Emma (perf): Exactly. We'll post a run summary thread with raw CSV + notebook. Targeting Wed 15:00 UTC. Any blockers?
Noah (sre): No blockers from infra side. All set. :thumbsup:
Kevin (ml): No blockers from model side. :+1:
Sophia (runtime): Will confirm kernel pinning once deployed.
Maria (qa): Trace and harness ready after cleanup; will ping when uploaded.
Emma (perf): Awesome — thanks everyone. Please react if you want to be in the postmortem. :eyes: 
Noah (sre): Adding calendar invite for run window.
perf-bot: run-sched: scheduled multi-region loadtest at 1711342400 (Wed 15:00 UTC)
Emma (perf): I'll start a results thread after the run with p50/p95 tables + per-region kernel breakdown and failover latency curves.
